newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 11.

text.p: Monsanto Co is thinking about selling or spinning off its chemical operations and concentrate on its agricultural biotechnology businesses, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
- U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation has charged 45 promoters, brokers and company officials involved in bribes to get customers to invest in penny stocks.
- Ford Motor Co will restructure its international automotive operations and create a unit to make parts.
- Tensions between General Motors Corp and union workers involves the company's plans to pit its Delphi parts-making operation against outside suppliers.
- Olin Corp agreed to sell its chemical business to ARCO Chemical Co for $565 million with plans to spin off its aerospace and ordnance operations.
- U.S. shoppers bought fewer apparel items, leading to slower sales growth for retailers in September.
- Loewen Group Inc rejected a share offer made by rival funeral home operator Service Corp International and filed suit against it, saying the proposal would hurt competition.
- Time Warner Inc completed its purchase of Turner Broadcasting System Inc.
- Microsoft Corp introduced its refurbished on-line service.
- General Electric Co reported a profit increase of 11 percent to $1.79 billion.
- J.P. Morgan & Co's quarterly profit fell 23 percent to $276 million which includes a $42 million charge.
- U.S. Continental Airlines Inc ordered 60 Boeing 737 jets for $2 billion.
- Aetna Inc plans $307 million in charges from job cuts following its purchase of U.S. Healthcare.
- A pact is near to allow the production of digital video-disk players without the risk of lawsuits over copyright infringement.
- American Express Co is returning to the brokerage business as it begins to promote its Financial Direct service that allows clients to invest by mail or phone.
- U.S. bond market particpants seem to be beginning to doubt that prices should be at such high levels given the lack of any real clues about the state of the country's economy.
